newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends higher on N. Dakota dryness.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends higher on N. Dakota dryness.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures settled slightly higher in light volumes amid uncertainty over weather forecasts in dry areas of North Dakota, traders said.

Drought conditions in western North Dakota have raised concern about damage to emerging spring wheat there. Some forecasts issued Wednesday called for rains by the end of the weekend, but the market was apprehensive.
"We're not going to break until we actually see rain," a MGE trader said at the midsession.
Traders said volumes were slack ahead of the Thursday release of USDA's June Supply/Demand and winter wheat production reports.
MGE spring wheat settled one to 2-1/4 cents per bushel higher, with July up 2-1/2 cents at $4.09-3/4. New crop September settled up one cent at $4.03.
Country Hedging was a featured player, selling 1.1 million July. Prudential sold close to a million July bushels.
